glossary.definition: A tax set at a fixed amount for each parcel of property (or for each room or square foot). A local government needs two-thirds of voters to approve one.
glossary.quote: With the approval of two-thirds of voters, local governments may impose a tax on all parcels in their jurisdiction (or a subset of parcels in their jurisdiction). Local governments typically set parcel taxes at fixed amounts per parcel (or fixed amounts per room or per square foot of the parcel).

glossary.definition: A separate local government that runs public schools. Berkeley Unified School District is governed by its own elected School Board, which adopts the district's budget.

questions.question: Is this everything the City of Berkeley spends?

paragraphs.text: Yes, for the City government. These pages show the City of Berkeley's own budget: {allFunds} across all its funds in {year}. Of that, {generalFund} is the [General Fund](glossary:General Fund (GF)), the City's main account for day-to-day services.
Public schools in Berkeley are run by Berkeley Unified School District (BUSD), a separate government. Its School Board has five elected directors and adopts the district's own budget.

cites.quote: The Berkeley Unified School District Board of Education, also called the School Board, is comprised of five elected directors
adopting policies, curriculum, and the District’s budget

paragraphs.text: So school spending isn't in the City's numbers. [BUSD publishes its budget on its own site](https://www.berkeleyschools.net/departments/business-services-division/berkeley-unified-budget/).

cites.quote: Each year before June 30 the School Board is required by law to pass a balanced budget.

paragraphs.text: Other governments serve Berkeley too. Each has its own budget, separate from the City's, so none of their spending is on these pages.

questions.question: Where does my property tax go?

paragraphs.text: The basic 1% property tax is pooled by the county and divided under state law among the county, cities, schools and [special districts](glossary:Special district).

cites.quote: Your county auditor pools your 1 percent rate tax payment, as well as payments from other property owners in your county, into a single countywide pot.
State law directs how your county auditor distributes the revenue in the countywide pot.
your county auditor sets aside this $1,000 for your city, county, schools, and special districts.

paragraphs.text: On top of that, voters approve extra taxes for particular governments, and that money goes to them, not the City. BUSD's three school [parcel taxes](glossary:Parcel tax) bring in $68.8M in 2026-27.

cites.quote: The second largest funding source comes from local parcel tax Measures, which provide a total of $68.8 million
For the 2026-27 fiscal year, the Berkeley Unified School District's (BUSD) combined General Fund is projected to receive $248.2 million in revenue.
There are three parcel tax Measures

paragraphs.text: The {propertyTax} in property tax on these pages is only the City's share.

questions.question: Does the City pay for the schools?

paragraphs.text: BUSD's budget names where its money comes from: state school funding (LCFF), Berkeley's school parcel taxes, restricted federal, state and local revenues, and other state money. The City of Berkeley isn't on that list.

cites.quote: The primary source of funding is State revenue from the Local Control Funding Formula (LCFF)
The second largest funding source comes from local parcel tax Measures
is projected from Restricted Federal, State, and Local revenues, which must be spent on specific programs
Finally, Other Unrestricted State program revenue totals $4.5 million

paragraphs.text: We haven't checked every line of the City's full budget, so small City grants to school programs can't be ruled out.
